binders: p is a nonnegative real number.
hp0 is a proof that 0 < p.
hp1 is a proof that p < 1.
hN is a proof that 0 < N.
hypotheses: The success parameter p is strictly positive.
The success parameter p is strictly less than 1; this also supplies p ≤ 1 to the probability constructions.
The number of trials N is strictly positive.
conclusions: The pushforward of the PMF on Boolean vectors Fin N → Bool under the function counting true coordinates is equal, as a PMF on Nat, to the standard binomial PMF with parameter p and N trials after its Fin (N+1) support is mapped to natural-number values.
mathematical_definitions: The success-count function sends f : Fin N → Bool to the cardinality of {i : Fin N | f i = true}.
The Boolean-vector PMF assigns an outcome f the product over i : Fin N of p when f i is true and 1-p when f i is false.
The natural-number-valued binomial PMF is obtained by mapping each i : Fin (N+1) in the standard binomial PMF to i.val : Nat.
Mapping a PMF along a function means taking the pushforward distribution of that function.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a success probability p strictly between 0 and 1 and a positive number N of independent Boolean trials, the distribution of the number of true outcomes is exactly the binomial distribution with parameters N and p, viewed as a probability mass function on the natural numbers.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is restricted to 0 < p < 1, excluding the degenerate endpoint parameters p = 0 and p = 1 even though the underlying PMF definitions require only p ≤ 1.
The proposition is restricted to N > 0, excluding the zero-trial case.

The hypotheses hp0 and hN do not occur in the elaborated equality itself; they only restrict the quantified cases, so the implication is vacuous whenever either strict-positivity premise is unavailable.
The proof object hp1 affects the displayed terms only through le_of_lt hp1, which supplies the p ≤ 1 argument used by both PMF constructions.
ambiguities: The packet exposes the one-level construction of the Boolean-vector PMF but omits internal proof terms marked by ellipses; these omissions concern well-definedness and normalization rather than the stated distributional meaning.

The displayed body of LocalDef002 names its weight function differently from the prepared local dependency label LocalDef005, but the provided type and product formula determine the intended Bernoulli product-weight semantics.
No independence predicate appears as a separate hypothesis; independence is encoded directly by the product form of the Boolean-vector weights.
